chunks: Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) encamped during the Expedition of Dhat al-Riqa under a tree on the edge of a valley. A flood came and separated him from his companions. A man from the Polytheists saw it, and the Muslims were standing on the edge of the valley waiting for the flood to subside. So a man from the Polythe flood to subside. So a man from the Polytheists said to his people, 'I will kill Muhammad.' He came and attacked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the sword, then said, 'Who will save you from me, O Muhammad?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'My Lord and your Lord.' So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) blew him off his horse, and he fell on his back. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood up, took the sword, and sat on his chest, and said, 'Who will save you from me, O Ghawrath?' He said, 'Your benevolence and generosity, O Muhammad.' So he (peace be upon him) left him. He stood up saying, 'By Allah, you are better than me and more generous.'
ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) was attacked by Ghawrath during the flood at Dhat al-Riqa?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kafi highlights the divine protection of the Prophet during the Expedition of Dhat al-Riqa, where the angel Jibraeel (AS) physically intervened to save him from the polytheist Ghawrath. The incident underscores the interplay between human agency and divine will, as the Prophet’s calm declaration of monotheism preceded the miraculous rescue, ultimately leading to Ghawrath’s recognition of the Prophet’s superior character and generosity.
